explainedBy: The analyst points at the compound model while Brennan weighs it: the CIA had nine months to deliberate over Abbottabad.

storyboard.claim: The pushback: the Abbottabad decision had nine months of patient, funded deliberation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst pointing at the walled compound model, Brennan watching, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the honest pushback announced in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The model and the room show what that slow deliberation looked like.

explainedBy: Johnson argues the coast question with his wife, who is unconvinced: his own choice took years of debate.

storyboard.claim: L'Enfant's planning took years, and Johnson's coast debate with his wife took years too.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Johnson talking to his worried wife at the kitchen table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Second example of a decision with plenty of time.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the debate as two people, one making the case and one doubting.

explainedBy: A clock beside the listener: what all those cases had was time.

storyboard.claim: All of those cases had a massive luxury of time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener beside a clock.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what the previous examples share.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the clock shows time; 'luxury' is carried by the text.

callout.text: No war room for most of us

explainedBy: The listener alone in his kitchen, slumped: no analyst team, no war room, no nine months.
noVisual: There is no way to draw the absence of a team and a war room; the lone, slumped listener contrasts with the staffed room of 349.

storyboard.claim: Most of us do not get analysts, a war room and nine months.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener alone and slumped, worried.
storyboard.onScreenText: Most of us do not get
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the cases to the viewer's real situation.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the contrast with 349's room is carried by being alone.

explainedBy: The small business owner holds his wallet at midnight, worried: he must decide how to make payroll tomorrow.

storyboard.claim: What good are these tools to a small business owner deciding about payroll at midnight?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener holding a wallet, worried, in the kitchen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the listener into a concrete crisis.
storyboard.addedInformation: The wallet names the money problem behind the decision.

explainedBy: The same owner, still holding the wallet, now faces the clock: the bank deadline looms at 8 a.m.

storyboard.claim: A screaming toddler, no sleep, and a bank deadline at 8 a.m.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The clock appears beside the owner, whose face turns afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the deadline clock is added and worry turns to fear.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock makes the deadline pressure visible.

explainedBy: A lunch plate in front of the relaxed listener: you do not build an influence diagram to decide what to eat for lunch.

storyboard.claim: You do not use the elaborate tools for every decision, like lunch or a midnight crisis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener at ease beside a dinner plate.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The reframe: the tools are not for everyday choices.
storyboard.addedInformation: The plate is the narrator's own example of a choice too small for the tools.

explainedBy: A flow: use the tools on massive choices when there is time, and that practice builds the muscle.

storyboard.claim: Use divergence, values mapping and scenarios on massive choices so you train your brain in peace.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: Massive choices -> Building the muscle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the mechanism behind the reframe.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows cause and effect: big decisions are the training ground.

explainedBy: The listener points to the third path in the fork: the training teaches the brain to invent third options.

storyboard.claim: You are training your brain to see hidden profiles and invent third options instinctively.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener pointing at the fork with a third path straight ahead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: What the muscle is trained to do.
storyboard.addedInformation: The third path shows what a 'third option' is.

explainedBy: Back in the midnight kitchen with the wallet and the clock: the training is for the moment the crisis hits.

storyboard.claim: It becomes muscle memory, for when the midnight crisis hits and there is no time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The owner again with the wallet and the clock, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the crisis scene from 353-354 to test the training.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the training back to the concrete crisis.

explainedBy: The same owner under the same clock stays calm instead of panicking: he no longer locks into a narrow A-or-B binary.

storyboard.claim: Your brain's default is no longer to panic and lock into option A or option B.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same stage; the worried face turns calm while 'Option A or option B' is struck.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the face calms and the binary is rejected.
storyboard.addedInformation: The calm face under the deadline shows panic did not come.

explainedBy: In the same crisis the owner now points to the third path: his rewired brain defaults to a wider view.

storyboard.claim: The brain defaults to seeking a wider perspective even in a split second.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same kitchen; the clock gives way to the fork with a third path, the owner points at it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of the sequence: from crisis to the wider option.
storyboard.addedInformation: The third path replaces the A/B binary on screen.

explainedBy: The listener faces a storm on the horizon: the future is chaotic, so no telescope can predict it.
noVisual: No telescope in the vocabulary; the storm carries 'chaotic future' and the struck text carries the rejected telescope.

storyboard.claim: Far-sightedness is not a magical telescope that sees the future with perfect accuracy; the future is chaotic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener before a storm on the horizon; the telescope phrase is struck.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the redefinition.
storyboard.addedInformation: The storm shows why prediction fails.

callout.text: Trade the telescope for a wide lens

explainedBy: A two-bucket sort: trading the telescope (see further) for the wide-angle lens (see wider now).

storyboard.claim: Far-sightedness is the daily discipline to see wider in the present; trade the telescope for a wide-angle lens.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sorter: The telescope | Wide-angle lens.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the redefinition from 361.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the two ideas side by side as the trade.

callout.text: A toy jeep in a model

explainedBy: The analyst points at the compound model: the journey went from the toxic pond to the secure room and its model of Pakistan.

storyboard.claim: We started at a toxic pond in Manhattan and went to a secure room with a toy jeep in a 3D model.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst pointing at the walled compound model.
storyboard.onScreenText: A toy jeep in a model
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recap of the journey begins.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the pond is not drawn; the model recalls the Abbottabad case.

explainedBy: Darwin and George Eliot seated at their desks with Darwin's two-column list: every case is linked by deliberative choice.

storyboard.claim: We sat at the desks of Darwin and Eliot; all these moments are linked by deliberative choice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin and Eliot seated, with the pros and cons list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the recap and names the thread.
storyboard.addedInformation: The list recalls Darwin's marriage decision at his desk.

explainedBy: The listener, warm and talking: a thank-you and one last thought before going back to the day.
noVisual: Pure sign-off commentary; no event to show.

storyboard.claim: Thanks for doing the deep work; one final thought.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener talking, happy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition to the closing idea.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: commentary only.

explainedBy: The listener slumps afraid beside the two-column list: we agonize over the columns, terrified of choosing wrong.

storyboard.claim: We spend our lives terrified of the wrong choice, agonizing over the columns on the legal pad.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener afraid and slumped beside the pros and cons list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the closing thought.
storyboard.addedInformation: The list is the literal columns the narration names.

explainedBy: Still before the list, the listener looks up surprised: maybe the defining decisions are not about picking a column at all.

storyboard.claim: What if the greatest decisions are not about picking the right option at all?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same stage; the afraid slump lifts into a surprised face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the face changes as the question turns.
storyboard.addedInformation: The list stays, so the question is about it.

explainedBy: The list gives way to the fork with a third path, and the listener points at it: throw out A and B and invent option C.

storyboard.claim: Throw out option A and B, look at the blank space on the map, and invent option C.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same stage; the pros and cons list is replaced by the fork with a third path; the listener points.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of the closing sequence: from two columns to the third path.
storyboard.addedInformation: The third path shows option C replacing the binary.
